evidence.claims: Disclaimers are present (index.html:192,199; README Disclaimers), not-affiliated wording is present, and the matrix and caps match Turo. But the headline claim on every surface is that Turo's US host share 'now depends on' plan AND booking window (README.md:21-23, index.html:15 and :186 FAQ, how-much-does-turo-take-from-hosts.html:29-30 and :102, llms.txt:3, VENTURE.yaml description). Turo's help page says this applies only 'in some US locations', the nine markets listed. No file in the venture mentions the market restriction (grep for austin/market/select: no hit). The guide's answer 'Turo takes between 0% and 35%' (how-much-...html:102) is wrong for hosts outside those markets, who face 10/20/30%. 'Every number ... exposed as an adjustable input' (README.md:62, calc.mjs:20-23) is not backed by the UI. 'Restructured ... around March 2026 into three named earnings plans' (README.md:21) conflates the 31 March 2026 variable-share pilot with the plans, which already existed.
evidence.fitness: Job: 'what will this trip pay me, and which plan should I pick'. A host in one of the nine variable-share markets can do it, short of delivery/Extras income. A host anywhere else, who is most US hosts, is shown a booking-window table that does not apply to them and a per-trip figure that is wrong unless they happen to pick 3-13 days. The plan-vs-damage-cap comparison is useful for everyone.
evidence.domain: Compared with Turo's published US earnings-plan terms (fetched). Correct: host share applies to trip price plus additional distance, additional usage and late return fees; the share locks at booking; caps are $250/$1,500/$2,750. Departs: (1) the variable share is applied nationwide instead of in nine markets; (2) delivery and Extras income, split at host share in the US, is not modelled; (3) incidental reimbursements (fuel, tolls, cleaning) paid at 100% are not mentioned, so 'Turo's cut' is fine but total trip income is understated. A power host would catch (1) within minutes.

defects.what: The booking-window matrix is applied to every US host, but Turo uses it only in nine markets (Austin, Dallas, Detroit, Las Vegas, Maui, Philadelphia, Phoenix, San Diego, Seattle); elsewhere the share is flat 70/80/90%. A host outside those markets gets a wrong payout for 3 of 4 window choices (Balanced, 28+ days, $350: 315.00 vs Turo 280.00), with no warning.

Headline copy says Turo's US host share 'now depends on' plan AND booking window, and the guide says Turo takes '0% to 35%'. Neither mentions that this is a nine-market rule; outside those markets Turo takes 10/20/30%.
'Every number ... exposed as an adjustable input' is unbacked: the UI has no host-share or cap inputs, only plan/window selects.
Delivery fee and Extras income, which Turo splits at the plan's host share for US hosts, cannot be entered, so a host who delivers or sells Extras understates the split-eligible amount.
Only 3 of 12 host-share cells and none of the damage caps are pinned by tests; changing a Peace of Mind cell or cap leaves all 54 tests green.
README dev command runs 3 of the 6 test files (omits share, and the two guide-page tests).

verdict: The arithmetic is right and the 12-cell table and damage caps match Turo's own help center exactly (check.mjs, 12/12). But Turo applies that booking-window table only in nine US markets, and nothing in the venture says so. Most US hosts are flat 70/80/90%, and the tool asks them for a booking window that does not affect their share; for 3 of 4 answers it then shows a wrong payout (Balanced, 28+ days, $350: 315 vs 280). The headline claim on every page repeats the same universality, and 'adjustable inputs' are claimed but not built. Delivery/Extras income is not modelled, and 2 of 4 seeded data mutants survived. Below the bar on correctness, claims and verification; the fix (a market toggle that uses the 3-13 column as the flat rate, copy naming the nine markets, a delivery/Extras field, tests pinning all 12 cells) is small.
